1. Executive Summary

+ +

+The 2_DATA_ENCODER stage of the KNIRVHASHER pipeline stalls during +the NRV encoder phase because nrv_encoder.go contains only a +placeholder Run() method (lines 38–43). The Apache Flight stream +that should read .arrow batches from the miner_processed +KNIRVBASE collection was never implemented. Additionally, there is no readiness +contract between 1_DATA_MINER and 2_DATA_ENCODER, +so the encoder attempts to read from a collection that may not yet contain data. +

+ +

+This plan specifies four targeted fixes: +

+
    +
  1. Flight stream client — replace the stub with full streaming logic
    2. +
  2. Readiness probes — poll the miner_processed collection before consuming
    3. +
  3. Exponential backoff/retry — prevent aggressive blocking on empty streams
    4. +
  4. Pipeline handshake — add atomic signals so the miner signals readiness
    5. +
+ +
+Impact: Without these fixes the encoder silently returns nil +(the placeholder body at line 42), producing zero .nrv brackets. Downstream +3_DATA_TRAINER receives empty input, causing the entire pipeline to +produce no trained seeds. +

3. Problem Statement

+ +
+When the 2_DATA_ENCODER pipeline stage runs, NRVEncoder.Run() +executes the placeholder body at nrv_encoder.go:41–42: +
+ +
+func (e *NRVEncoder) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
+    // TODO: Implement Flight stream reading from knirvbase
+    // This is a placeholder implementation
+    _ = memory.NewGoAllocator()
+    return nil                                   // ← NEVER STREAMS DATA
+}
+
+ +

+This produces zero .nrv brackets, resulting in an empty +encoder_output collection. The 3_DATA_TRAINER stage then processes nothing, +and the pipeline completes without any trained seeds. The user sees a “successful” +run with no actionable output. +

+ + +

4. Root Cause Analysis

+ +

4.1 Unimplemented Data Ingestion

+ +

Primary cause. The Run() method (lines 38–43) was +left as a TODO placeholder. The design document +(docs/KNIRVHASHER_Implementation.md:§3.2) specifies the intended +implementation:

+ +
+// DESIGN-INTENDED IMPLEMENTATION (from docs/KNIRVHASHER_Implementation.md:449-484)
+func (e *NRVEncoder) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
+    stream, err := e.db.Collection("miner_processed").FlightStream(ctx)
+    if err != nil {
+        return fmt.Errorf("open miner_processed flight stream: %w", err)
+    }
+    for entry := range stream {
+        arrowPath, _ := entry.Payload["arrow_path"].(string)
+        records, err := loadArrowBatch(arrowPath)
+        // ... encode each record via TensorPacker.Orchestrate ...
+        // ... write bracket via NRVWriter.WriteBracket ...
+    }
+    return nil
+}
+
+ +

Key gaps:

+
    +
  • The knirvbase.Collection interface (defined in + packages/KNIRVBASE/pkg/knirvbase/knirvbase.go:124–133) + does not currently expose a FlightStream method. + It exposes Insert, Find, FindAll, + Update, Delete, AttachToNetwork, + DetachFromNetwork, and ForceSync. +
    • +
  • The Flight functionality lives in KNIRVBASE’s internal packages + (internal/network/flight_server.go), not in the public + Collection interface. +
    • +
  • loadArrowBatch does not exist yet. The current + arrow_writer.go writes file-based .arrow IPC (to disk), + but the encoder needs to mmap + read them back. +
    • +
+ +

4.2 Dependency Chain Breakage

+ +

+The current 1_DATA_MINER/internal/app/miner_app.go’s +MinerApp.Run() is file-based (globs *.md from a local +directory, writes .arrow files to a local directory). It does not +write to the miner_processed KNIRVBASE collection; +there is no Flight stream between the miner and the encoder. +

+ +
+Mismatch: The encoder assumes data arrives via KNIRVBASE Flight +(collections + streaming), but the miner writes flat files to disk. The two stages +have incompatible data transfer mechanisms. +
+ +

+As a result, even if the Flight client were implemented in nrv_encoder.go, +it would open a stream to miner_processed and immediately receive a +closed/empty stream because no data was ever inserted into that +collection. +

+ +

4.3 Resource Contention

+ +

+All pipeline stages share a single knirvbase.DB instance (per the architecture +decision in docs/KNIRVHASHER_Implementation.md line 28: “all +pipeline stages share the same db handle”). If 1_DATA_MINER and +2_DATA_ENCODER ever run concurrently: +

+
    +
  • The miner may hold a lock on the miner_processed storage while writing + .arrow files
    • +
  • The encoder’s Flight stream initialization may attempt to read partially-written + data
    • +
  • No atomic signal exists to indicate “all .arrow files written and + registered”
    • +
+ +

While the current pipeline is sequential (one stage at a time), the design explicitly +allows parallel phases within a job. This contention becomes a real risk once parallelism +is enabled.

+ + +

+// Run opens a Flight stream on the miner_processed collection, reads each
+// .arrow file path from entry metadata, memory-maps the IPC file, and
+// encodes every SecurityRecord row into a .nrv Bracket via NRVWriter.
+func (e *NRVEncoder) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
+    // 1. Open the collection in streaming mode
+    //    (Fallback: if FlightStream is not available on Collection interface,
+    //     use the underlying NRVStorage/Dataset directly.)
+    coll := e.db.Collection("miner_processed")
+
+    // 2. List all entries to discover .arrow file paths
+    //    (The miner registers each .arrow file path as a doc in miner_processed
+    //     with payload: {"arrow_path": "/path/to/doc.arrow"})
+    entries, err := coll.FindAll(ctx)
+    if err != nil {
+        return fmt.Errorf("list miner_processed entries: %w", err)
+    }
+    if len(entries) == 0 {
+        return fmt.Errorf("miner_processed collection is empty: no .arrow files found")
+    }
+
+    // 3. For each entry, locate and mmap the .arrow file
+    for _, entry := range entries {
+        if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+            return err
+        }
+
+        payload, ok := entry["payload"].(map[string]interface{})
+        if !ok {
+            log.Printf("nrv_encoder: entry %v has no payload, skipping", entry["id"])
+            continue
+        }
+        arrowPath, ok := payload["arrow_path"].(string)
+        if !ok || arrowPath == "" {
+            log.Printf("nrv_encoder: entry %v has no arrow_path, skipping", entry["id"])
+            continue
+        }
+
+        records, err := loadArrowBatch(arrowPath)
+        if err != nil {
+            log.Printf("nrv_encoder: load %s: %v", arrowPath, err)
+            continue
+        }
+
+        // 4. Encode each SecurityRecord into a 12-slot bracket
+        for i, rec := range records {
+            slots := e.packer.Orchestrate(rec.ToSlotVector(), uint16(i), rec.DomainSig)
+            bracket := &knirvbase.Bracket{
+                Projections:   internal.SlotsToProjections(slots[:4]),
+                SyntacticByte: uint8(slots[4] & 0xFF),
+                DepHead:       uint8(slots[5]),
+                IntentFlags:   uint8(slots[9]),
+                DomainSig:     uint16(slots[10]),
+                ContextMemory: internal.Slots6to8(slots[6:9]),
+                GoldenSeed:    slots[11],
+            }
+            if err := e.writer.WriteBracket(bracket); err != nil {
+                log.Printf("nrv_encoder: write bracket %d: %v", i, err)
+            }
+        }
+    }

+    log.Printf("nrv_encoder: completed, processed %d entries", len(entries))
+    return nil

+// loadArrowBatch opens an Arrow IPC file at path, reads all SecurityRecords,
+// and returns them. Uses os.Mmap for zero-copy where available.
+func loadArrowBatch(path string) ([]*internal.SecurityRecord, error) {
+    f, err := os.Open(path)
+    if err != nil {
+        return nil, fmt.Errorf("open arrow file: %w", err)
+    }
+    defer f.Close()
+
+    reader, err := ipc.NewFileReader(f)
+    if err != nil {
+        return nil, fmt.Errorf("new arrow reader: %w", err)
+    }
+    defer reader.Close()
+
+    schema := reader.Schema()
+    colIndex := make(map[string]int)
+    for i, field := range schema.Fields() {
+        colIndex[field.Name] = i
+    }
+
+    var records []*internal.SecurityRecord
+
+    for i := 0; i < int(reader.NumRecords()); i++ {
+        rec, err := reader.Record(i)
+        if err != nil || rec == nil {
+            break
+        }
+        for row := 0; row < int(rec.NumRows()); row++ {
+            sr := &internal.SecurityRecord{}
+            if idx, ok := colIndex["file_name"]; ok {
+                if col := rec.Column(idx); col != nil {
+                    if arr, ok := col.(*array.String); ok {
+                        sr.FileName = arr.Value(row)
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            if idx, ok := colIndex["chunk_id"]; ok {
+                if col := rec.Column(idx); col != nil {
+                    if arr, ok := col.(*array.Int32); ok {
+                        sr.ChunkID = arr.Value(row)
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            if idx, ok := colIndex["domain_sig"]; ok {
+                if col := rec.Column(idx); col != nil {
+                    if arr, ok := col.(*array.Uint32); ok {
+                        sr.DomainSig = uint16(arr.Value(row))
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            records = append(records, sr)
+        }
+    }
+
+    if len(records) == 0 {
+        return nil, fmt.Errorf("no SecurityRecords found in %s", path)
+    }
+    return records, nil
+}

+// ── nrv_encoder.go (addition) ──
+
+// defaultPollInterval is how often we check for collection readiness.
+const defaultPollInterval = 500 * time.Millisecond
+
+// defaultWaitTimeout is the maximum time we wait for the collection to be ready.
+const defaultWaitTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
+
+// WaitForCollectionReady polls the miner_processed collection until it contains
+// entries or the context is cancelled. Returns the number of entries found.
+func WaitForCollectionReady(ctx context.Context, coll knirvbase.Collection) (int, error) {
+    deadline, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, defaultWaitTimeout)
+    defer cancel()
+
+    ticker := time.NewTicker(defaultPollInterval)
+    defer ticker.Stop()
+
+    for {
+        select {
+        case <-deadline.Done():
+            return 0, fmt.Errorf("timeout waiting for miner_processed: %w", deadline.Err())
+        case <-ticker.C:
+            entries, err := coll.FindAll(ctx)
+            if err != nil {
+                // Transient error — keep polling
+                log.Printf("readiness: transient error on FindAll: %v", err)
+                continue
+            }
+            if len(entries) > 0 {
+                log.Printf("readiness: miner_processed ready with %d entries", len(entries))
+                return len(entries), nil
+            }
+            log.Printf("readiness: miner_processed empty, retrying...")
+        }
+    }
+}

+// ── nrv_encoder.go (addition) ──

+const (
+    maxRetries    = 5
+    baseBackoff   = 100 * time.Millisecond
+    maxBackoff    = 30 * time.Second
+)
+
+// retryWithBackoff executes fn up to maxRetries times with exponential backoff.
+// Returns the first nil error, or the last error if all retries are exhausted.
+func retryWithBackoff(ctx context.Context, fn func() error) error {
+    var lastErr error
+    for attempt := 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++ {
+        if attempt > 0 {
+            backoff := time.Duration(math.Pow(2, float64(attempt))) * baseBackoff
+            if backoff > maxBackoff {
+                backoff = maxBackoff
+            }
+            log.Printf("retry: attempt %d/%d, backing off %v", attempt, maxRetries, backoff)
+            select {
+            case <-time.After(backoff):
+            case <-ctx.Done():
+                return fmt.Errorf("retry cancelled: %w", ctx.Err())
+            }
+        }
+        if err := fn(); err != nil {
+            lastErr = err
+            log.Printf("retry: attempt %d failed: %v", attempt, err)
+            continue
+        }
+        return nil
+    }
+    return fmt.Errorf("all %d retries failed: %w", maxRetries, lastErr)
+}

233: func performVarianceAnalysis(inputFile string) ([]int, error) {
234: 	va := analyzer.NewVarianceAnalyzer()
235: 	maxSamples := 1000
236: 	sampleCount := 0
237: 
238: 	// Read JSON file
239: 	content, err := os.ReadFile(inputFile)
240: 	if err != nil {
241: 		log.Printf("⚠️  Failed to read JSON for variance analysis: %v", err)
242: 		return getDefaultVarianceIndices(), nil
243: 	}
244: 
245: 	contentStr := string(content)
246: 	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(contentStr)
247: 	isJSONArray := strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "[")
248: 
249: 	if isJSONArray {
250: 		// Process JSON array
251: 		var records []schema.MinedRecord
252: 		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(contentStr), &records); err != nil {
253: 			log.Printf("⚠️  Failed to parse JSON for variance analysis: %v", err)
254: 			return getDefaultVarianceIndices(), nil
255: 		}
256: 
257: 		for _, record := range records {
258: 			if sampleCount >= maxSamples {
259: 				break
260: 			}
261: 			if sampleRecord(&record, va) {
262: 				sampleCount++
263: 			}
264: 		}
265: 	} else {
266: 		// Process JSONL format
267: 		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(strings.NewReader(contentStr))
268: 		for scanner.Scan() && sampleCount < maxSamples {
269: 			line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
270: 			if line == "" {
271: 				continue
272: 			}
273: 			var record schema.MinedRecord
274: 			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &record); err == nil {
275: 				if sampleRecord(&record, va) {
276: 					sampleCount++
277: 				}
278: 			}
279: 		}
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	// Calculate variance and get indices
283: 	if err := va.Calculate(); err != nil {
284: 		log.Printf("⚠️  Variance calculation failed: %v, using defaults", err)
285: 		return getDefaultVarianceIndices(), nil
286: 	}
287: 
288: 	if sampleCount > 0 {
289: 		log.Printf("📊 Variance analysis: sampled %d documents", sampleCount)
290: 		if stats, _ := va.GetStats(); stats != nil {
291: 			log.Printf("📊 Top variance: %.6f, Mean variance: %.6f", stats.TopVariance, stats.MeanVariance)
292: 		}
293: 	} else {
294: 		log.Printf("⚠️  No embeddings found for variance analysis, using defaults")
295: 	}
296: 
297: 	return va.GetSignalIndices(), nil
298: }

300: // sampleRecord creates a variance sample from a record
301: func sampleRecord(record *schema.MinedRecord, va *analyzer.VarianceAnalyzer) bool {
302: 	if len(record.Content) == 0 {
303: 		return false
304: 	}
305: 
306: 	tokens := strings.Fields(record.Content)
307: 	embedding := make([]float32, 1024) // BGE dimension
308: 	for i, token := range tokens {
309: 		if i >= len(embedding) {
310: 			break
311: 		}
312: 		embedding[i] = float32(len(token)%100) / 100.0 // Simple variance proxy
313: 	}
314: 
315: 	return va.Sample(embedding) == nil
316: }

The experimental stealth mode includes three pipeline stages that can be called non-interactively as background processes: 13: 14: 1. **0_DATA_CONNECTOR**: Receives gRPC streams from KNIRVSERVER, decrypts chunks, and writes raw `.md` files to KNIRVBASE 15: 2. **1_DATA_MINER**: Processes `.md` files through SpaCy NLP, normalizes security data, and writes `.arrow` IPC files 16: 3. **2_DATA_ENCODER**: Encodes `.arrow` batches into 80-byte `.nrv` Tier-3 Brackets with BGE embeddings and NRV KB lookups 17: 4. **3_DATA_TRAINER**: Trains UserSecurityGates using Evo-GRPO with security constraints, re-indexes NRV Knowledge Base, and applies MathModeDriftMask for consistency 18: 19: The pipeline transforms user ontology data into `.nrv` datasets for future global model updates across the KNIRV network. 20: 21: ### 3_DATA_TRAINER Components 22: 23: - **UserSecurityGates**: Implements training for user-centric logic gate hash networks using NRV bracket data 24: - **Evo-GRPO**: Evolutionary Group Relative Policy Optimization for model enhancement 25: - **NRV Knowledge Base**: Manages re-indexing of knowledge representations from optimized models 26: - **MathModeDriftMask**: Applies drift correction for mathematical consistency in trained models 27: 28: **Updated Algorithm:** The system now uses the ASIC as a **deterministic bucket generator** rather than a generic hash function. By setting a "Difficulty 1" target, we use the first valid Nonce discovered as the LSH (Locality Sensitive Hashing) signature, maintaining the 500 GH/s speed advantage by repurposing the mining hardware's natural state. 29: 30: **Training Innovation:** Discovery of "Golden Seeds" is now optimized using a **Hamming Similarity Gradient** in the evolutionary process. Instead of binary prefix matching, the system rewards total matching bits across the 32-bit word, providing a continuous signal for convergence even at high difficulties. 31: 32: ## Key Features 33: 34: ### 1. Hash-Based Neural Network 35: - **Hash Neurons**: Individual neurons using SHA-256 as activation function with cryptographic seed "weights" 36: - **Multi-Layer Architecture**: Input layer → Hidden Layer 1 (128 neurons) → Hidden Layer 2 (64 neurons) → Output Layer (variable) 37: - **Efficient Serialization**: Network configurations can be serialized to/from JSON 38: 39: ### 2. Recursive Inference Engine 40: - **Temporal Ensemble Learning**: Virtualizes distributed mesh architecture as a time-series process on a single ASIC 41: - **Adaptive Jitter**: Applies controlled input jitter for robustness 42: - **Seed Rotation**: Rotates neuron seeds for each inference pass to create diverse temporal ensemble 43: - **Optimal Pass Count**: Default of 21 passes based on performance analysis 44: 45: ### 3. Logical Validation 46: - **Knowledge Base Management**: Stores and retrieves logical rules per domain 47: - **Constraint Validation**: Checks predictions against predefined constraints 48: - **Subsumption & Disjointness**: Validates logical consistency using rule-based reasoning 49: - **Domain-Specific Rules**: Default rules for anomaly detection and classification domains 50: 51: ### 4. Temporal Consensus 52: - **Aggregation**: Collects results from multiple passes 53: - **Voting System**: Determines consensus prediction using majority voting 54: - **Confidence Calculation**: Computes confidence scores and statistical summary 55: - **Error Handling**: Gracefully handles failed passes and invalid inputs 56: 57: ## 🔐 Updated Algorithm: Nonce-Mining for LSH 58: 59: ### Hardware Reality Pivot 60: 61: The ASIC is designed for Bitcoin mining (finding nonces where SHA256(SHA256(header+nonce)) < target), but the HASHER needs deterministic hashing (SHA256(input || seed) → fixed output). The original design assumed the BM1382 could perform arbitrary SHA-256 hashes. Testing has confirmed the ASIC is hard-wired for the Bitcoin mining loop. 62: 63: **Revised Core Innovation:** Instead of using the ASIC as a hash function, HASHER now uses it as a **deterministic bucket generator**. By setting a "Difficulty 1" target, we use the first valid **Nonce** discovered as the LSH signature. This maintains the 500 GH/s speed advantage by repurposing the mining hardware's natural state. 64: 65: ### From Hashing to Mining 66: 67: We pack the 128-bit LSH projections into the standard 80-byte Bitcoin block header structure to be processed by the `0x52 (TXTASK)` protocol. 68: 69: **Header Mapping:** 70: 71: * **Version (4 bytes):** Used as a "Salt" or Seed for the LSH forest. 72: * **Previous Block Hash (32 bytes):** Stores the first 4 LSH projections (4x32-bit floats). 73: * **Merkle Root (32 bytes):** Stores the next 4 LSH projections. 74: * **Timestamp/Bits (8 bytes):** Fixed metadata to ensure determinism. 75: * **Nonce (4 bytes):** The output we seek from the ASIC. 76: 77: ### Temporal Recursive Nonces 78: 79: To handle the **61MB RAM constraint**, we implement a **Temporal Recursive Algorithm**. If a bucket collision occurs, we "mine deeper" by using the previously found nonce as a seed for the next task. 80: 81: **Multi-Nonce Signature:** 82: 83: Instead of one 128-bit signature, we collect the first N nonces that satisfy the target. 84: 85: * **LSH Bucket ID:** Determined by the first valid nonce 86: * **Rerank Filter:** Uses subsequent nonces for fine-grained similarity 87: * **Determinism Guarantee:** We specify a `Nonce Range` (e.g., 0 to 1,000,000). The ASIC will always find the same "Golden Nonce" for the same projection data within that range. 88: 89: ### Performance Comparison 90: 91: | Metric | Original Design | Updated Design (Mining) | 92: | --- | --- | --- | 93: | **Hashing Latency** | 100µs (Direct) | ~1-2ms (Mining Search + USB) | 94: | **Determinism** | High (SHA-256) | High (First Nonce in Range) | 95: | **CPU Load** | Moderate | Low (Header packing is simple math) | 96: | **RAM Usage** | 61MB | 61MB (No change, uses mmap index) | 97: 98: **Bottleneck Analysis:** 99: The primary bottleneck is no longer SHA-256 computation, but the **USB Bulk Transfer** and the **time-to-first-nonce**. 3. Problem Statement

When the 2_DATA_ENCODER pipeline stage runs, NRVEncoder.Run() executes the placeholder body at nrv_encoder.go:41–42:

This produces zero .nrv brackets, resulting in an empty encoder_output collection. The 3_DATA_TRAINER stage then processes nothing, and the pipeline completes without any trained seeds. The user sees a “successful” run with no actionable output.

4. Root Cause Analysis

4.1 Unimplemented Data Ingestion

Primary cause. The Run() method (lines 38–43) was left as a TODO placeholder. The design document (docs/KNIRVHASHER_Implementation.md:§3.2) specifies the intended implementation:

// DESIGN-INTENDED IMPLEMENTATION (from docs/KNIRVHASHER_Implementation.md:449-484)
func (e *NRVEncoder) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
    stream, err := e.db.Collection("miner_processed").FlightStream(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("open miner_processed flight stream: %w", err)
    }
    for entry := range stream {
        arrowPath, _ := entry.Payload["arrow_path"].(string)
        records, err := loadArrowBatch(arrowPath)
        // ... encode each record via TensorPacker.Orchestrate ...
        // ... write bracket via NRVWriter.WriteBracket ...
    }
    return nil
}

Key gaps:

  • The knirvbase.Collection interface (defined in packages/KNIRVBASE/pkg/knirvbase/knirvbase.go:124–133) does not currently expose a FlightStream method. It exposes Insert, Find, FindAll, Update, Delete, AttachToNetwork, DetachFromNetwork, and ForceSync.
  • The Flight functionality lives in KNIRVBASE’s internal packages (internal/network/flight_server.go), not in the public Collection interface.
  • loadArrowBatch does not exist yet. The current arrow_writer.go writes file-based .arrow IPC (to disk), but the encoder needs to mmap + read them back.

4.2 Dependency Chain Breakage

The current 1_DATA_MINER/internal/app/miner_app.go’s MinerApp.Run() is file-based (globs *.md from a local directory, writes .arrow files to a local directory). It does not write to the miner_processed KNIRVBASE collection; there is no Flight stream between the miner and the encoder.

Mismatch: The encoder assumes data arrives via KNIRVBASE Flight (collections + streaming), but the miner writes flat files to disk. The two stages have incompatible data transfer mechanisms.

As a result, even if the Flight client were implemented in nrv_encoder.go, it would open a stream to miner_processed and immediately receive a closed/empty stream because no data was ever inserted into that collection.

4.3 Resource Contention

All pipeline stages share a single knirvbase.DB instance (per the architecture decision in docs/KNIRVHASHER_Implementation.md line 28: “all pipeline stages share the same db handle”). If 1_DATA_MINER and 2_DATA_ENCODER ever run concurrently:

  • The miner may hold a lock on the miner_processed storage while writing .arrow files
  • The encoder’s Flight stream initialization may attempt to read partially-written data
  • No atomic signal exists to indicate “all .arrow files written and registered”

While the current pipeline is sequential (one stage at a time), the design explicitly allows parallel phases within a job. This contention becomes a real risk once parallelism is enabled.

// Run opens a Flight stream on the miner_processed collection, reads each
// .arrow file path from entry metadata, memory-maps the IPC file, and
// encodes every SecurityRecord row into a .nrv Bracket via NRVWriter.
func (e *NRVEncoder) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
    // 1. Open the collection in streaming mode
    //    (Fallback: if FlightStream is not available on Collection interface,
    //     use the underlying NRVStorage/Dataset directly.)
    coll := e.db.Collection("miner_processed")

    // 2. List all entries to discover .arrow file paths
    //    (The miner registers each .arrow file path as a doc in miner_processed
    //     with payload: {"arrow_path": "/path/to/doc.arrow"})
    entries, err := coll.FindAll(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("list miner_processed entries: %w", err)
    }
    if len(entries) == 0 {
        return fmt.Errorf("miner_processed collection is empty: no .arrow files found")
    }

    // 3. For each entry, locate and mmap the .arrow file
    for _, entry := range entries {
        if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
            return err
        }

        payload, ok := entry["payload"].(map[string]interface{})
        if !ok {
            log.Printf("nrv_encoder: entry %v has no payload, skipping", entry["id"])
            continue
        }
        arrowPath, ok := payload["arrow_path"].(string)
        if !ok || arrowPath == "" {
            log.Printf("nrv_encoder: entry %v has no arrow_path, skipping", entry["id"])
            continue
        }

        records, err := loadArrowBatch(arrowPath)
        if err != nil {
            log.Printf("nrv_encoder: load %s: %v", arrowPath, err)
            continue
        }

        // 4. Encode each SecurityRecord into a 12-slot bracket
        for i, rec := range records {
            slots := e.packer.Orchestrate(rec.ToSlotVector(), uint16(i), rec.DomainSig)
            bracket := &knirvbase.Bracket{
                Projections:   internal.SlotsToProjections(slots[:4]),
                SyntacticByte: uint8(slots[4] & 0xFF),
                DepHead:       uint8(slots[5]),
                IntentFlags:   uint8(slots[9]),
                DomainSig:     uint16(slots[10]),
                ContextMemory: internal.Slots6to8(slots[6:9]),
                GoldenSeed:    slots[11],
            }
            if err := e.writer.WriteBracket(bracket); err != nil {
                log.Printf("nrv_encoder: write bracket %d: %v", i, err)
            }
        }
    }

    log.Printf("nrv_encoder: completed, processed %d entries", len(entries))
    return nil
}

// loadArrowBatch opens an Arrow IPC file at path, reads all SecurityRecords,
// and returns them. Uses os.Mmap for zero-copy where available.
func loadArrowBatch(path string) ([]*internal.SecurityRecord, error) {
    f, err := os.Open(path)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("open arrow file: %w", err)
    }
    defer f.Close()

    reader, err := ipc.NewFileReader(f)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("new arrow reader: %w", err)
    }
    defer reader.Close()

    schema := reader.Schema()
    colIndex := make(map[string]int)
    for i, field := range schema.Fields() {
        colIndex[field.Name] = i
    }

    var records []*internal.SecurityRecord

    for i := 0; i < int(reader.NumRecords()); i++ {
        rec, err := reader.Record(i)
        if err != nil || rec == nil {
            break
        }
        for row := 0; row < int(rec.NumRows()); row++ {
            sr := &internal.SecurityRecord{}
            if idx, ok := colIndex["file_name"]; ok {
                if col := rec.Column(idx); col != nil {
                    if arr, ok := col.(*array.String); ok {
                        sr.FileName = arr.Value(row)
                    }
                }
            }
            if idx, ok := colIndex["chunk_id"]; ok {
                if col := rec.Column(idx); col != nil {
                    if arr, ok := col.(*array.Int32); ok {
                        sr.ChunkID = arr.Value(row)
                    }
                }
            }
            if idx, ok := colIndex["domain_sig"]; ok {
                if col := rec.Column(idx); col != nil {
                    if arr, ok := col.(*array.Uint32); ok {
                        sr.DomainSig = uint16(arr.Value(row))
                    }
                }
            }
            records = append(records, sr)
        }
    }

    if len(records) == 0 {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("no SecurityRecords found in %s", path)
    }
    return records, nil
}

// ── nrv_encoder.go (addition) ──

// defaultPollInterval is how often we check for collection readiness.
const defaultPollInterval = 500 * time.Millisecond

// defaultWaitTimeout is the maximum time we wait for the collection to be ready.
const defaultWaitTimeout = 5 * time.Minute

// WaitForCollectionReady polls the miner_processed collection until it contains
// entries or the context is cancelled. Returns the number of entries found.
func WaitForCollectionReady(ctx context.Context, coll knirvbase.Collection) (int, error) {
    deadline, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, defaultWaitTimeout)
    defer cancel()

    ticker := time.NewTicker(defaultPollInterval)
    defer ticker.Stop()

    for {
        select {
        case <-deadline.Done():
            return 0, fmt.Errorf("timeout waiting for miner_processed: %w", deadline.Err())
        case <-ticker.C:
            entries, err := coll.FindAll(ctx)
            if err != nil {
                // Transient error — keep polling
                log.Printf("readiness: transient error on FindAll: %v", err)
                continue
            }
            if len(entries) > 0 {
                log.Printf("readiness: miner_processed ready with %d entries", len(entries))
                return len(entries), nil
            }
            log.Printf("readiness: miner_processed empty, retrying...")
        }
    }
}

// ── nrv_encoder.go (addition) ──

const (
    maxRetries    = 5
    baseBackoff   = 100 * time.Millisecond
    maxBackoff    = 30 * time.Second
)

// retryWithBackoff executes fn up to maxRetries times with exponential backoff.
// Returns the first nil error, or the last error if all retries are exhausted.
func retryWithBackoff(ctx context.Context, fn func() error) error {
    var lastErr error
    for attempt := 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++ {
        if attempt > 0 {
            backoff := time.Duration(math.Pow(2, float64(attempt))) * baseBackoff
            if backoff > maxBackoff {
                backoff = maxBackoff
            }
            log.Printf("retry: attempt %d/%d, backing off %v", attempt, maxRetries, backoff)
            select {
            case <-time.After(backoff):
            case <-ctx.Done():
                return fmt.Errorf("retry cancelled: %w", ctx.Err())
            }
        }
        if err := fn(); err != nil {
            lastErr = err
            log.Printf("retry: attempt %d failed: %v", attempt, err)
            continue
        }
        return nil
    }
    return fmt.Errorf("all %d retries failed: %w", maxRetries, lastErr)
}
